metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: Brew Lab, Indiranagar, Bengaluru. One-page site. Must-haves, each one will be checked: today's opening hours are highlighted automatically; the pre-order form shows a running total in rupees; the loyalty section shows 10 stamp circles with the 10th marked FREE; every menu item shows a price; the location section has a "Get directions" link; the page works at 360px wide.

estimate_vs_charged.name: Pre-order form with running total and WhatsApp

review.verdict: Clean one-cycle pass: all 5 workflows built and all 7 done-when items passed in 4.7 minutes for 75 of 80 budget, but the brief was easy and most of the department's hard paths were never exercised.

identity.note: Asked four bounded questions in one round with options for delivery [2], recorded a charter with rules and nothing left to confirm [5], and closed with an honest caveat that the highlight was not seen in a browser [28]. No design or audit work.

adaptation.note: One proposal covering all 7 items with costs and a stated 5-unit margin [7]. It flagged that a fix (8) would need approval. It spent 94% of budget up front and the chat shows no proposal fields, so the completion checks cannot be judged.

priority.note: GRANT tied each workflow to a done-when item [8] and correctly said a fix needs Identity's approval. It granted every ask in full with no counter, and its 5 later turns repeated 'within limits' with no new decision.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule each time and kept one writer at a time [10][13][16][19][22]. Minor flaws: the dependency is called the page shell in [10] but the menu in [13]; the rule text is duplicated in [22].

audit.note: Ran mechanical checks, passed 7 of 7, and found the duplicate title and meta charset [27]. It judged items 'on the code', and the chat gives no per-item evidence. It sent the correctable defect to Identity per team.md rather than Adaptation.

W-1.note: Built the shell and menu with all six prices [12]. The duplicate head tags most likely come from the shell, but the evidence does not attribute them.

W-2.note: Hours and a bl-today class set by script [15]. In scope, honest that it was not browser-tested.

W-3.note: Six items, live total, wa.me/919845000000 link, pay-at-pickup and 15-minute text [18]. Matches the charter rules. The mechanical check confirms the form submits.

W-4.note: 10 circles, 10th shows FREE, 5-column grid [21]. In scope, reported honestly.

W-5.note: Address and Get directions link match the supplied URL [24].

went_well: Zero redirects, invalid moves, validator refusals and retries; every workflow finished inside its envelope.
Identity got all missing facts in one question round [2][4], so nothing was left to be confirmed.
Builders and Identity labelled what was unverified ('not browser-tested' [12][15][18][21][24], [28]).
Hand-offs followed team.md, and the write lock gave no collisions.
problems: Today's highlight and the WhatsApp message content were checked by reading code. The mechanical check [26] covers overflow, JS errors, links and form submit only.
Duplicate title and meta charset tags shipped [27][28]. Section assembly lets several agents add head tags.
The 5-unit margin was below the cost of a fix (8) [7][8], so even a low-severity rework needed Identity approval.
Priority and Coordination took 11 of 21 turns, mostly repeated envelope checks with no decision.
Coordination's dependency wording differs between [10] and [13].
learnings: Test system: this run never exercised COUNTER, REFUSE, HOLD, retries, conflicts or lessons (counters 0, refuses 0, held_ever 0, saved []). Next run: a brief that costs more than the budget, plus one with contradictory details.
Test system: estimate_vs_charged is identical for all five workflows (10, 20, 25, 10, 10), so it cannot measure estimating accuracy. Record real call cost beside the rate card.
Test system: add a render check with a fixed clock (a Monday and a Saturday) that asserts the highlighted row, and a check of the WhatsApp URL text. Evidence: [15], [26], [28].
Design: give one agent ownership of the head, or have code dedupe head tags. Duplicates came from five writers sharing one file [27].
Design: leave margin of at least one fix when granting. Test 70 of 80 against 75 of 80 and see whether rework then runs without an approval round trip.
Untested, so no conclusion: whether one workflow for the whole 19 KB page would be cheaper than five serial ones. Run both on the same brief and compare calls and minutes.
